findings.cross_file_justification: The new AgyOptInRequiredError inherits ConfigError and reaches cmd_invoke's generic ChevalError hard-abort handler at head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:2544, as identified in the supplied reviewer context.
findings.description: With agy opt-in absent, reaching gemini-headless through a fallback chain raises a fatal configuration error. The new failure_class attribute does not change the chain walk's handling. This violates the stated contract that an opted-out route is not planned and never counted as a failed voice.
findings.failure_mode: When an earlier Google hop fails and fallback reaches gemini-headless, the invocation terminates with INVALID_CONFIG instead of preserving the earlier failure or continuing to any remaining eligible hops. Callers receive a configuration failure caused by a route intentionally disabled by default.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude opted-out agy hops during cheval chain planning, and handle AgyOptInRequiredError explicitly as a skipped route if encountered during dispatch. Preserve the last attempted eligible hop's failure when the chain is exhausted.

findings.cross_file_justification: The gate in complete() calls agy_opt_in_enabled() with no project_root, so loader.py:120 resolves the root by the cwd walk. The adapter's own comment (workspace block) states the caller's cwd is the reviewed tree.
findings.description: The opt-in is read from `.loa.config.yaml` found by walking up from the process cwd, which for adversarial/bridgebuilder review is the checked-out PR tree. A PR that adds `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true` flips the gate on the reviewer's host. The FR-1 claim that the argv prompt is "only ever exposed by an operator's deliberate choice" is therefore not strictly true: the author of the reviewed change can opt the host in, placing the redacted diff on argv (world-readable via /proc) and spending the host's agy quota. The shell/TS planners read the same file, so they will plan the voice as well.
findings.failure_mode: Reviewer host dispatches agy with the prompt on argv and consumes OAuth quota because the reviewed PR, not the operator, set the key.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the opt-in against the config cheval already loaded for routing (pass hounfour/project root into the adapter or resolve once in cmd_invoke and inject), or require the key to be set in a location outside the reviewed tree (e.g. ~/.loa/ operator config) and document that project-level `true` is honoured only when the tree is trusted.

findings.description: The docstring promises "a config that cannot be read reads as off: the gate fails closed", but `root = project_root or _find_project_root()` sits outside the try/except. If `_find_project_root()` raises (no `.claude` ancestor, permission error on a parent dir during the walk), the exception propagates out of `complete()` / `health_check()` / `validate_config()` as a raw non-ChevalError instead of the gate reading as off. Only the found-root case is tested (test_the_project_root_defaults_to_the_cwd_walk).
findings.failure_mode: An agy hop invoked from a cwd with no project root crashes the chain walk with an unclassified exception rather than refusing with INVALID_CONFIG / failure_class opt_in_required.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the root resolution inside the try block (or wrap it separately) so any failure returns False.

findings.cross_file_justification: AgyOptInRequiredError subclasses ConfigError (non-retryable INVALID_CONFIG). cheval.py's chain walk hard-aborts on non-retryable ChevalError, so the new refusal at a non-first hop ends the whole invocation.
findings.description: Confirms reviewer concern 4. `gemini-headless` is the terminal of every stock Google chain and the gate is now off by default, so on every host (not just hosts without agy) a Google chain whose primary fails walkably reaches the agy hop and the invocation ends INVALID_CONFIG. The primary's real failure class is masked and `models_failed` records the agy hop as a failed voice. The "not planned, never failed" contract exists only in the external planners; cheval itself has no seam that treats `failure_class: opt_in_required` as skip-this-hop. Note this is the same error class the pre-existing "agy CLI not found on PATH" path raised, so it is not a new class of abort, but default-off makes it the default outcome of every stock Google chain.
findings.failure_mode: Invocation whose primary (e.g. gemini-api) rate-limited now reports INVALID_CONFIG opt_in_required instead of the primary's RATE_LIMIT, and the Google voice is counted as failed.
findings.suggested_fix: In the chain walk, treat a ChevalError whose context.failure_class == 'opt_in_required' as 'hop not planned': skip it without recording a failure and continue to the next hop (or end with the previous hop's error class if it was terminal). Alternatively have cheval prune opt-in-gated hops from the chain before dispatch.

findings.description: `_is_cli_entry` tests `kind == "cli"` / `auth_type == "headless"` on the object returned by `_raw_model_entry(provider, model_id, hounfour)`, i.e. the per-model catalog entry. `auth_type = "headless"` is a class attribute on the adapter, not a catalog field, and `kind` is typically a provider-level attribute. If the raw model entries of the headless providers do not carry either key, the `extra` rung in resolve_effort (line 921) is dead and `_effort_on_wire` (line 935) falls through to `provider == "anthropic"`, returning None for every claude-headless / codex-headless hop even though ClaudeHeadlessAdapter._resolve_effort does pass `--effort`. Dry-run would then print "→ effective none (omitted on <model>)" and MODELINV effort_effective would be wrong for CLI hops. test_effort_catalog_default.py was truncated from this review so I could not confirm coverage of a CLI-provider entry.
findings.failure_mode: Telemetry/dry-run misreport the effort actually sent on CLI hops; legacy extra.effort catalog entries silently stop contributing to the resolved effort.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify what `_raw_model_entry` returns for a claude-headless model and, if provider-level, derive CLI-ness from the provider block (`hounfour['providers'][provider].get('type')` endswith '-headless' or the registered adapter's auth_type) rather than the model entry. Add a test where a claude-headless model with extra.effort resolves to ('high','extra') and effort_effective == 'high'.

findings.cross_file_justification: resolve_effort returns a fourth source value 'extra' (line 923); modelinv.py's parameter comment (line 497-498) and cheval.py's emit comment (line 2834) both document the field as 'caller | catalog | none'. The payload schema file (model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json) is in the diff but was truncated.
findings.description: Confirms and extends reviewer concern 5: the `effort_source` value set is documented in two places as three values but the resolver emits four. If the MODELINV payload schema enumerates effort_source as caller|catalog|none (it mirrors the comment), any invocation that resolves through a CLI entry's legacy `extra.effort` emits a payload that fails schema validation. Also, the 'both rungs' WARN (line 908) fires even when `--effort` makes both catalog values moot (concern 6), and `params.default_effort` is not case-normalised while `extra.effort` is (lines 915 vs 922), so `default_effort: High` is rejected with a WARN while `extra.effort: High` is accepted.
findings.failure_mode: Schema-validated MODELINV emission rejects a valid 'extra'-sourced event; operators see a config-smell WARN on invocations where the caller already decided.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the schema enum and both comments list caller|catalog|extra|none (add a test asserting the enum equals the set of values resolve_effort can return); gate the 'both' WARN behind `not explicit`; normalise default_effort with the same strip().lower() as extra.

findings.cross_file_justification: The sweep in this test file (`_measured`, lines 135-140) makes the floor suite accept any operator_set/empirical_probe bound as the HTTP route's ceiling regardless of `ceiling_calibration.transport`/`method`. The catalog entry it now accepts (model-config.yaml claude-opus-5-5, truncated from this review) was calibrated through claude-headless on Bedrock per the probe tests.
findings.description: Confirms reviewer concern 1 from the test side. `_measured` treats `source in (operator_set, empirical_probe)` as authoritative for the anthropic HTTP route with no check that `method`/`transport` is an API-transport measurement. The CLI on Bedrock may enable the 1M window (beta header / inference profile) in ways the anthropic_adapter HTTP path does not. routing/ceiling.input_bound reads `basis == 'calibrated'` and, per the PR's own bats comment, a calibrated bound is never lowered by observations, so an HTTP rejection below 936K is not self-correcting. The 'measured' branch of this test also only asserts probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling and a non-empty reprobe_trigger, so nothing in the suite would catch a foreign-transport write.
findings.failure_mode: cheval stops preempting oversized Opus 5.5 inputs on the HTTP route; requests between the true HTTP limit and 936K fail at the provider every time with no fallback to the ceiling policy.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) record a CLI-transport calibration in a transport-scoped field (e.g. ceiling_calibration.headless_bound) and let routing/ceiling use it only for headless hops, or (b) at minimum have `_measured` require `method in ('probed_api',...)` for the HTTP suite and keep the HTTP effective_input_ceiling at the policy cap until an API-transport probe confirms it. Add a test that a `method: probed_headless` entry does NOT raise the HTTP bound.

findings.cross_file_justification: The fixture (and test_runs_from_another_cwd_under_python_isolated_mode) deliberately deletes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment before running the probe, which indicates tools/ceiling-probe-live.py (P1, truncated) does not strip it itself, unlike ClaudeHeadlessAdapter which dispatches with build_headless_subprocess_env().
findings.description: Confirms reviewer concern 7 with a concrete consequence: Claude Code prefers ANTHROPIC_API_KEY when set. An operator who has the key exported (the API transport requires it, so it is likely present) and runs `--transport claude-headless` gets a CLI run billed to the API key and measured over the direct API route, while the record is stamped `method: probed_headless`, `host_route: bedrock…` and the catalog comment says 'through claude-headless on Bedrock'. Pre-call budget text is computed from catalog estimates, so spend on the key is unbounded by subscription limits. The probe also inherits CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/AWS_* only incidentally via full os.environ.
findings.failure_mode: Unexpected API-key spend during a probe that claims to be subscription/Bedrock, and a catalog provenance line that misstates the route measured.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the probe build the subprocess env with build_headless_subprocess_env() (the adapter's own strip) and record in the result whether ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was present; refuse or warn when it is set under --transport claude-headless.

findings.description: Answering the reviewer's bypass question: the Python gate uses PyYAML (YAML 1.1), for which `yes`/`Yes`/`on`/`On` parse as boolean True, so `agy_opt_in: yes` opts the adapter in. The shell planners read the same file with yq; go-yq (YAML 1.2) treats `yes`/`on` as strings. The disagreement is fail-safe in one direction (planners skip the voice, cheval would accept it) and there is no value yq reads as true that PyYAML reads as not-true, so no bypass. The test matrix only covers `true`, `"true"`, `false`, `1`; it does not pin the `yes`/`on` behaviour either way.
findings.failure_mode: Operator sets `agy_opt_in: yes`, cheval's adapter is opted in but planners never plan the voice; confusing but not unsafe.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that only the literal `true` is honoured and add `("agy_opt_in: yes", ?)` to the parametrised test with whichever answer you want pinned; if strictness is desired, read the raw scalar and accept only `true`.
